segments.he: כְּשֶׁמַּכְרִיחַ אֶת עַצְמוֹ לְדַבֵּר אֲזַי הַתּוֹרָה מוּדַעַת לוֹ מַה
segments.en: Therefore He sends us in every generation wondrous Tzaddikim who in their sublime wisdom plant in our minds never to despair of mercy in any way, and plant in our hearts a wondrous strengthening to always strengthen ourselves in prayer, whatever the situation — and through this the redemption will come speedily. And this is the aspect of the power of the Purim miracle — for Haman the wicked, may his name be blotted out, is the aspect of the kelipah that sought to overpower at the end of the Babylonian exile to delay the redemption and weaken the hearts of Yisrael from multiplying prayer, since they saw that the time promised for their redemption after seventy years had already passed and they were still not redeemed. And therefore Haman sought to plant the error in the heart that there was no longer hope. But Yisrael through their prayers arouse His mercy little by little each time, until speedily He will be aroused, as it were, from His sleep — in the aspect of "Then Hashem awoke as one sleeping" [Tehillim 78:65] — and redeem us speedily. For in truth there is no sleep before Him, Heaven forbid — as it is written: "Behold, He neither slumbers nor sleeps, the Guardian of Yisrael" [Tehillim 121:4] — only that because of the attribute of strict law He, as it were, hides His face from us, until it appears as if He is sleeping. And we are obligated to pray and cry out to Him always and to arouse His mercy as one who is aroused from sleep. Until through the abundance of prayers He is fully aroused and returns to us and has mercy — but Haman said: "their G-d is asleep" as if it were impossible to arouse Him further, Heaven forbid. For Haman made himself an idol — which is the opposite of the service of prayer which is the aspect of faith. For he is the aspect of the flaw of prayer — the aspect of the kelipah that weakens a person's heart from strengthening himself in prayer, since they see the prolonging of exile and cry out without being saved. And the Torah commanded us to remember the deed of Amalek — "remember what Amalek did to you" [Devarim 25:17] — karcha from the language of mikreh [accident], the aspect of the flaw of the bris, which is the primary evil inclination. And karcha is also from the language of coldness — that he cools the heart of a person from strengthening himself in prayer, which must be with the warmth of holiness in the aspect of "my heart was hot within me... I spoke with my tongue."

segments.he: בְּעֵת שֶׁאִישׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי נִכְנָס לְהִתְפַּלֵּל תְּפִלָּתוֹ וְשִׂיחָתוֹ לִפְנֵי ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּזְכֶּה לְהִתְקָרֵב אֵלָיו וּלְקַיֵּם תּוֹרָתוֹ וּמִצְוֹתָיו וְרוֹצֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת מֵהַתּוֹרָה תְּפִלָּה אֲבָל עֲדַיִן אֵין מִלָּה בִּלְשׁוֹנוֹ לְדַבֵּר.
segments.en: It emerges that the kelipah of Haman-Amalek is the aspect of the kelipah that weakens and slackens the heart of a person from praying — because they see the prolonging of troubles and exile — as described above. And therefore his downfall came through Mordechai and Esther, who are the aspect of the totality of the prayers of the true Tzaddik and of the Kneses Yisrael [Assembly of Yisrael]. For Mordechai the Jew is the aspect of the Tzaddik of the generation, who is the aspect of Moshiach, who is the aspect of fragrance — encompassing all the prayers. For all his warfare and all his conquest are through prayer, as explained in the Torah teaching above. For Mordechai is the aspect of besamim rosh, mar deror — whose Aramaic translation is marei dachya [master of purity], as our Rabbis expounded — meaning the aspect of the head and root of all the prayers, which are the aspect of fragrance, the aspect of Moshiach. For he is the aspect of besamim rosh — rosh specifically, the aspect of head and firstborn, which is the service of prayer, opposed to the aspect of reishis goyim Amalek [first of the nations is Amalek] which is the aspect of laxity in prayer, as if nothing has yet been accomplished.

segments.he: כִּי עֲדַיִן אֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ דַּרְכֵי וְסִימָנֵי הַתּוֹרָה וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ אֵיךְ לְהִתְפַּלֵּל וּלְדַבֵּר וְלָשִׂיחַ. אֲזַי בְּחִינַת רָחֵל שֶׁהִיא בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה בְּחִינַת חִדּוּשִׁין דְּאוֹרַיְתָא שֶׁמֵּהֶם נִמְשָׁכִין הַדְּרָכִים לַעֲשׂוֹת מִתּוֹרוֹת תְּפִלּוֹת כַּנַּ"ל. אֲזַי הִיא בְּעַצְמָהּ מְרַחֶמֶת עַל אִישׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי הַזֶּה הַמִּתְפַּלֵּל שֶׁהוּא בִּבְחִינַת לֵאָה כַּנַּ"ל. וּמוֹסֶֶרֶת לוֹ הַסִּימָנִים וְהַדְּרָכִים שֶׁל הַתּוֹרָה וּמְדַבֶּרֶת בְּעַצְמָהּ עִם דּוֹדָהּ בְּחִינַת יַעֲקב בְּחִינַת כְּלַל שׁרֶשׁ הַתּוֹרָה. כְּדֵי שֶׁיּוּכַל לַעֲשׂוֹת מֵהַתּוֹרָה תְּפִלָּה. כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּזְדַּוְּגוּ תּוֹרָה וּתְפִלָּה יַחַד. כְּדֵי שֶׁיּוֹלִידוּ מַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים. וְזֶה בְּחִינַת הַדִּבּוּרִים הַנִּשְׁפָּעִים לָאָדָם בְּעֵת שֶׁנִּכְנָס לְהִתְבּוֹדֵד וּלְפָרֵשׁ שִׂיחָתוֹ לִפְנֵי ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁבִּתְחִלָּה אֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ שׁוּם דִּבּוּר לְדַבֵּר. וּכְשֶׁהוּא חָזָק בְּדַעְתּוֹ וּמַכְרִיחַ עַצְמוֹ אַף עַל פִּי כֵן לְדַבֵּר. אֲזַי עַל פִּי רב בָּאִים לוֹ דִּבּוּרִים שֶׁלּא עָלָה עַל דַּעְתּוֹ שֶׁיְּדַבֵּר אוֹתָם. וְאֵלּוּ הַדִּבּוּרִים נִשְׁלָחִים לוֹ מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם וְנִמְשָׁכִים מִבְּחִינָה הַנַּ"ל. (שָׁם אוֹת לב):
segments.en: And Mordechai — the aspect of besamim rosh — strengthens the heart of every single person in Yisrael to begin anew each time and strengthen oneself in prayer, for we have already accomplished much but still need to accomplish very much more, until the building is complete — the building of the Tabernacle, to bring Hashem back to us face to face. And compared to the very greatness of the salvations still needed, we have not yet begun to pray properly at all. And even so, Hashem has already helped us very greatly. But every single day we must begin to strengthen and overpower ourselves in prayer anew — for His greatness is without limit. And He strengthens our hearts to trust in His kindness always and to strengthen ourselves in prayer always — for no prayer is ever in vain, Heaven forbid. Rather every single prayer makes an impression and from them the stature of the Shechinah is built, which is the aspect of the building of the Beis HaMikdash — until the full measure of its stature is complete, then His compassion will be stirred and He will return to us.
